utility.notes: CPAU is the City of Palo Alto's own municipal utility, providing electricity, water, wastewater, natural gas, and fiber optics, with its own net-metering rules and rebate programs distinct from PG&E. Palo Alto is not served by PG&E for electric delivery.

value.name: City of Palo Alto Utilities (CPAU)
value.notes: CPAU is a vertically-integrated municipal utility (like Riverside Public Utilities, Banning Electric Utility, Burbank Water and Power, and Glendale Water and Power) — it generates/procures and delivers its own power rather than sitting alongside a separate CCA. No Community Choice Aggregator was found serving Palo Alto in the sources reviewed this session.

permit_authority.value: City of Palo Alto Utilities (CPAU) / Development Services
permit_authority.notes: Palo Alto requires a two-step process: Electric Utilities Pre-Approval from CPAU, then a building/electrical permit from Development Services.

interconnection_url.notes: CPAU's own PV Permitting and Interconnection page; Palo Alto's interconnection ('Permission to Operate') process is run by CPAU itself rather than an outside IOU.

value.notes: Typical approval time is 3 business days, though complex projects requiring structural review may take longer. Separately, the utility interconnection process (Permission to Operate) can take 2-12 weeks after the system passes inspection; the system cannot legally export power to the grid until PTO is granted.

value.program_or_pathway: Electric Utilities Pre-Approval (CPAU) then building/electrical permit; SolarApp+ available for qualifying stand-alone roof-mounted PV systems without an electrical service upgrade
other_conditions: Solar requires both a building/electrical permit from the city AND a separate utility interconnection agreement from CPAU — these are separate processes with separate timelines
